USA-NA-AIO[edit]

The USA-NA-AIO (United States North American Artificial Intelligence Olympiad) is the premier competition for students in the US and Canada to compete in AI. The contest is split into 3 parts to qualify for two international competitions: The IAIO (International AI Olympiad) and IOAI (International Olympiad of AI). The main difference between the two is the IAIO is known as the winter AI Olympiad and accepts 4 students from each country, while the IOAI keeps its name and accepts 8 students from each country.

The contest is based on Google's Colabatory, a fast, free Python shell and interface, known for its easy-to-use format and high compatibility.

USA-NA-AIO Round 1[edit]

This is the first round of the contest. It requires no qualification. Because it is such a new Olympiad, the contest managers are still trying out new question formats: In 2025, there were 3 questions, split into many parts. In 2026, there were 9 questions with a few parts each. In each year, there are a maximum of 300 total points scoreable. The cutoff this year was 98.

The contest is held at local testing sites and sometimes at home, all of which with camera and screen supervision.

USA-NA-AIO Round 2[edit]

This is the second round, from which participants can enter through qualifying from Round 1. It is held at MIT, although this year they are holding it both at MIT and Harvard. It is significantly harder than Round 1.

Team USA Training Camp[edit]

Those with a high enough score at Round 2 qualify for the Camp. Here, participants are tasked with solving home, on-site, and team tasks. To keep things fun and fair, USA AIO has implemented a cosine-similarity based selector: [Team USA Formation]

Topics Covered[edit]

The USA AIO often covers many subjects, such as linear algebra, calculus, statistics, probability in the math area, as well as basic Python (NumPy, MatPlotLib, Pandas, Seaborn).

The more advanced subjects include SciKit, PyTorch, and learning about different types of AI models and how they work, and training and building them yourself.
